column5:
The internal carotid artery is divided into 4 parts
(segments): cervical, petrous, cavernous and cerebral.
By clinical classification it is divided into seven
segments: the cervical part corresponds to segment C I;
the petrous part to the petrous segment C II and the
lacerum segment C III; the cavernous part to segment
C IV; between the cavernous and cerebral parts lies the
clinoid segment C V; the cerebral part consists of the
supraclinoid segment C VI and the terminal segment
C VII.
